brief: Wave-0 entity flag predicate over 28-byte records.
decl: std::uint32_t entity_flag(std::span<const std::byte> table, std::uint32_t index);
notes: The original reads the table base from global 0x8e3ab8; the reconstruction
takes it explicitly, consistent with emulated-address handling.
Verified against the original by tools.w0_int_leaf_oracle.
The host form takes the table bytes; the original reads the base from global 0x8e3ab8, an emulated address never dereferenced on the host.

bookkeeping.scope: Complete body. The predicate reads the flag byte of the 28-byte record at table_base[index*28+0x1a] and returns its low bit as 0 or 1, matching the original across 12 oracle cases over three table offsets and five indices.
bookkeeping.supported_domain: Indices whose 28-byte record lies inside the supplied table; an out-of-range index is rejected rather than emulated.
unresolved: Which entity system owns the 28-byte record and its bit-0 meaning.
bookkeeping.acceptance: Met: 8 fresh original-execution cases matched bit-exact by the native runner; self-test registered in ctest. See docs/recovery/cell-comparisons.md.
